_readme: Relevance judgments: for each query, the page(s) a good search engine should
return. These are human decisions, not measurements — they are the opinion
the metrics are scored against, so they are worth arguing with and editing.
The corpus (quotes.toscrape.com) has a natural ground truth, which is why it
can be judged honestly rather than by taste:
an author's name  -> that author's page, which carries their biography
a tag's name      -> the page collecting the quotes under that tag
Targets are URLs, not doc IDs, because IDs are assigned by sorted filename
and shift whenever the corpus changes. A URL means the same thing after a
A query may list several acceptable targets. 'edison' is genuinely ambiguous
between the man and the tag, so both count as correct.
